questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Being able to practice french, as well as the high hopes for the academic level.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The information at the "Reunion Erasmus" was quite informing. But all the small things that was "nice to know", or just basic information was usually quite hard to come by.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: As mentioned above, the "Reunion Erasmus" was the main source of information upon arrival.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Fondation Danoise in Cité Universitaire is a great place to apply for housing. It wasn't too hard to apply, and the facilites are great. It's right next to the RER, and very close to Sorbonne

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It isn't quite possible too live on campus, so it's just the basic living conditions. Fondation Danoise wasn't too expensive, but if you want a studio apartment closer to the centre of Paris, you have to empty your pockets.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
For someone not being native to Sorbonne, all the neccessary information seemed scattered all over the place and very disorganized. Therefore a lot of the information concering registration was a bit confusing. 
We had to meet up physically at the UFR to get the paper needed to enroll for classes. After that, there was a given interval where you could  give back the paper, with the desired courses.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You are very much on your own at Sorbonne, if you don't know anybody there. The people in the administration surely are not very keen on helping, unless they forced to do so.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It was easy getting the right CM, but getting the right seminars(TD) connected to the CM, was a bit of a puzzle. Especially because the Erasmus students had to enroll after all the normal students. This meant that a lot of the TD's were already full, which can make quite a mess, because you have to make your own schedule.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't be intimidated by the administration, and don't be afraid to seek out other Erasmus students. They are probably just as confused as you are, but it makes the confusion less stressfull.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level compared to UCPH wasn't that different. Of course, the courses being in french, certainly introduced a new problem of understanding, which is not present in UCPH. But all in all, the level seems to match.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: For a non-native french speaker, the fact that the professors only talked, and didn't use any forms of visual presentations certainly increased the difficulty. A normal lecture would normally consist of the professor entering the room, opening a book, and talking for the whole duration. No to little interaction, which really differs from UCPH. Therefore there are not many ways in which the style of teaching compares.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
1. Philosophie Politique
2. Philosophie Comparée
3. Historie de Philosophie
4. Métaphysique
5. Logique
6. Philosophie de la connasaince
7. Competances transversales

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Every course with M. Pascal Ludwig was very nice. A very intelligent professor with more modern ways of teaching.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I didn't look too much into that. But compared to UCPH, the student life was not really present at Sorbonne. I know that there were some sports clubs, but i dont have any other information.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Don't have any recommendations.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Literally just walk around Paris. Paris is an amazing city, and even being here for 6 months wasn't enough to explore every part of the city.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was very easy. The only difference is having to speak french everywhere you go, but that is something that settles in fast.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: It doesn't even seem that the local student socialize a lot with each other. There aren't a lot of opportunities to do so.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not anything in particular.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The quality of the food and wine I must admit. A lot of the gastronomical experiences were just amazing.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Have a lot of patience
2. Practice your writing-hand (and hand-writing) before arrival
3. Don't lose hope, even though it is quite easy to do

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't be scared to ask the professors for information. They are usually always happy to help.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Probably the improvement of french.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The whole system of Sorbonne can be very unorganized, which really decreases the morale. The way of exams were very different compared to UCPH. A lot of the exams were physical and relied entirely on memory.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
